chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from some of our companions from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'Whatever We have made permissible for him, if he acquires it from the deeds/wealth of the oppressors, it is permissible for him; and whatever We have forbidden from that, it is forbidden.'

key_terms.أَعْمَالِ: deeds or actions, here referring to the fruits or wealth acquired through them
key_terms.اَلظَّالِمِينَ: the oppressors, those who unjustly acquire or hold wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wealth taken from oppressors according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the principle of *al-ziyadat* (additions), clarifying that the Imam’s specific declaration determines the permissibility of wealth acquired from oppressors. This underscores the Imam’s legislative authority to adapt rulings based on context, ensuring that wealth taken from tyrants is not automatically deemed illicit unless explicitly prohibited. This principle is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the flexibility of *halal* and *haram* statuses regarding spoils or compensation from unjust rulers.
